preamble: Raising of a nasalized mid front vowel /ẽ/ to oral /i/, combining denasalization with raising. It is documented in Ersu (Ersuic, Sichuan), where Yu's reconstruction of Proto-Ersuic has a rhyme *-ẽ that surfaces as -i in Ersu but as -e or -ɤ in the Lizu varieties. Yu orders this 'final raising of *-je and *-ẽ to -i' after Ersu's apicalization of old *-i, which is why the new -i rhymes are not apicalized. No other well-documented case of this exact change is known, so it is a rare, language-specific development.

examples.note: Compare Mianning Lizu tsʰe and Lǚsū (Kala Lizu) tshe³⁵, which keep a mid vowel.
Lǚsū (Kala Lizu) ndze³⁵ keeps the mid vowel.
The raised -i is not apicalized after the sibilant, unlike Ersu reflexes of old *-i, showing the raising came after apicalization.

sources: Yu, D. (2012). Proto-Ersuic. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley. https://linguistics.berkeley.edu/~dom/proto-ersuic.pdf
